transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-14 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Malik Chen (AlphaHealth Head of AI), Sara Dubois (Platform Eng), Lina Torres (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, I'll run the commercial side, and Priya is our SE who'll drive the benchmarks. Malik, Lina, Sara, thanks for joining.
[00:18] Malik: Thanks. we're excited, we've been looking at cost modelling for the triage assistant use case — want to make sure a POC shows us economics before wide rollout.
[00:30] Priya: Great. my goal today is to pin success criteria, get your workload sizing, and align on benchmark configs — tokens, batching, caching, timelines. I'll also sketch per-token estimates so you can see ballpark unit economics.
[01:05] Lina: top priorities are latency for live triage (under 300ms ideally), cost per conversational session under $0.05, and false positive rate for triage under 12%.
[01:30] Sara: from infra side we have a constrained budget for the POC — target spend is $2k for the 3-week POC. we can add more if benchmarks justify it, but want to avoid surprises.
[01:55] Jordan: good constraints. i'll flag that $2k is tight but doable with careful model selection + batching + caching. will share assumptions.
[02:20] Priya: quick clarifying q: what's your expected QPS during peak?
[02:30] Malik: Typical peak is ~8 rps for triage, but we expect bursty traffic—maybe 25 rps for short minutes. overall daily sessions ~30k.
[02:50] Priya: ok that's helpful. for cost modeling I need avg tokens per session, do you have estimates?
[03:05] Lina: for initial triage it's multi-turn but short: avg prompt 120 tokens, model reply 80 tokens, so ~200 tokens/session. For the follow-up summarization workflow we have longer context — up to 1,800 tokens per job but those run asynchronously.
[03:35] Priya: perfect. i'll model two workload profiles: "Realtime triage" (200 tokens/session, p95 latency target 300ms) and "Async summarization" (1,800 tokens/job, relaxed latency but throughput focused).
[04:00] Jordan: from a pricing lens, their budget implies we should aim for per-token raw cost below $0.0009 to keep daily spend in range — that's a rough target.
[04:20] Malik: can you explain how batching and caching affect that number?
[04:30] Priya: sure. two levers: batching increases GPU utilization so amortizes fixed compute overhead per request — it reduces effective per-token cost but increases tail latency. caching (prefix or snippet-level) eliminates repeated prompt decoding for repeated patterns; for triage there's a lot of repeated question templates so caching is high-impact.
[04:55] Sara: are you talking about KV cache or full response cache? we've got concerns about PII and caching.
[05:05] Priya: good callout. we use prefix/KV caching for internal model state (not persistent user PII), and you can opt-in only for non-sensitive fields. we also support encrypted in-flight caching and TTLs so you can evict after X minutes.
[05:35] Malik: ok, so safe to use on the triage prompts which are templated.
[05:42] Priya: exactly. in our cost model i'll show three scenarios: conservative (no caching), expected (20-30% token reduction via prefix KV cache), and optimistic (50% reduction for extremely templated flows).
[06:05] Jordan: also model quantized model variants — int8 or 4-bit where quality doesn't drop. that can cut GPU cost by 30–40% compared to fp16 depending on hardware.
[06:25] Lina: do you have numbers for typical per-token cost per model family?
[06:33] Priya: ballparks: larger 70B fp16 on premium GPUs ~ $0.0020 token, int8 variant ~ $0.0012 token. mid-size 13B fp16 ~ $0.0009 token, int8 ~ $0.0006. embedded cheaper models (distilled ~7B) around $0.00035–$0.0005. these are raw inference costs before batching gains and caching.
[07:05] Malik: those ranges are helpful. so for 200 tokens/session at $0.0009 token that's $0.18/session raw? that seems high.
[07:18] Priya: careful—math: 200 tokens * $0.0009 = $0.18 yes that's raw compute. but with batching (amortize 30% lower) and caching (20–30% tokens cut) you can bring it down to ~$0.08–$0.10/session. then there's infra margin, network, and our platform fee.
[07:44] Jordan: we typically quote a final customer-visible unit that's platform-inclusive; for POC we'll show raw model spend + estimated infra and Redwood fee. goal: show you scenarios that meet your $0.05/session requirement — to get there we may need smaller model for initial triage or aggressive caching.
[08:05] Sara: what's the impact of continuous batching on latency? we can't exceed 300ms p95.
[08:15] Priya: batching adds queueing delay. if you batch up to 8 requests, mean amortized cost drops but p95 may increase 60–120ms depending on throughput. to hit 300ms p95 for triage we usually set max batch 4 and use low-latency kernels; also use warm KV cache and keep sequence length small. we'll include p95 latency estimates in the benchmark.
[08:45] Malik: timeline for POC?
[08:50] Jordan: we propose 3 weeks: Week 1 — benchmark setup and initial runs (model variants + baseline), Week 2 — integrate into your staging service and run realistic traffic, Week 3 — tuning and final run + handoff. Priya will own bench config.
[09:10] Priya: for benchmarking we'll need: a representative traffic replay (we prefer pcap-style JSON of prompt+metadata), a validation set for triage accuracy, and staging endpoints or ephemeral VPC peering. expect 4–6 hours of bench runs per model variant to collect stable metrics.
[09:40] Lina: we can produce anonymized replays but need to mask PHI. any tips?
[09:47] Priya: mask PHI client-side; for accuracy checks we can use label-only export. for latency/cost you can use synthetic tokens derived from distribution of lengths if privacy is hard.
[10:05] Jordan: also want to set clear success criteria now. what would AlphaHealth consider a POC win?
[10:12] Lina: three gates: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for realtime triage at target QPS, 2) per-session cost <= $0.05 on expected load, 3) triage quality comparable to current rules-based baseline (F1 delta >= +8%).
[10:36] Malik: add: security approval for VPC peering + SOC2 docs reviewed.
[10:42] Jordan: ok we'll include SOC2 + architecture diagrams in the package we send.
[10:48] Priya: for the bench configs i'm going to propose a matrix: models [13B fp16, 13B int8, 7B distilled], batching [1,4,8], caching [none, 25%, 50% effective token reduction], and route policy [hosted Redwood vs dedicated]. each cell yields cost, p95 latency, and accuracy.
[11:15] Sara: what about private deployment? we may eventually want private to meet compliance. how does that change unit economics?
[11:25] Priya: Private (VPC/air-gapped) increases fixed cost — reserved capacity or on-prem hardware cost. per-token raw can be lower at high utilization but requires commit. for a pilot of 30k sessions/day not worth reserved hardware; hosted or dedicated short-term rental is better. we'll show both projections.
[11:50] Malik: curious about automated fallback — could we route low-confidence triage to a cheaper model?
[11:58] Priya: yes, dynamic routing is part of the plan: primary model for high-confidence class, fallback to smaller cheaper model for low confidence, or a rules-based deferral. this can cut cost but adds complexity; we'll include simulation in the bench harness.
[12:20] Jordan: i want to call out two quick risk items: 1) annotation noise in your dataset can bias accuracy numbers, 2) PHI handling may limit caching. we'll document both.
[12:36] Lina: understood.
[12:40] Priya: now a short walkthrough of the benchmark script — it launches the model container, runs warmup tokens, starts traffic generator ramp to peak, and collects token counts, GPU utilization, latency histograms. we instrument batching metrics and cache hit rates.
[13:05] Malik: will you share the exact bench code?
[13:09] Priya: yes, open-source harness with small Redwood integration bits. I'll post link after the call.
[13:18] Jordan: back to pricing assumptions — i will attach a spreadsheet that has line items: model per-token cost, batch amortization factor, cache hit factor, infra markup, and Redwood platform fee. that'll give per-session and monthly projections.
[13:38] Sara: can you put a scenario where the per-session cost is under $0.05 using caching + small model? we want to see concrete path to that.
[13:47] Priya: yes, e.g., 7B distilled at $0.00045/token * 200 tokens = $0.09 raw; but with 50% caching reduces to $0.045; then batching and infra could keep it under $0.05 if platform fee is minimal — it's tight but feasible if cacheable.
[14:12] Malik: what about quality delta vs rules baseline? does 7B deliver that +8% F1?
[14:20] Priya: depends on fine-tuning. out-of-the-box may not reach +8%, but a small fine-tune on labeled triage data (50–100k examples) usually pushes it over. we'll estimate fine-tune effort and cost in the doc.
[14:41] Lina: do you support running fine-tune in POC window?
[14:45] Priya: yes, we can run a small supervised fine-tune or LoRA-style adapter during the POC week 2—we'll budget time and GPU. that's in the spreadsheet as a one-time cost.
[14:58] Jordan: let's nail down budget split: AlphaHealth has $2k hard cap for Redwood-hosted spend for POC; Redwood can add a dev-time credit. We'll propose an initial bench on shared infra that stays within $2k for first pass. If you want dedicated runs (full scale), we'll need additional commit.
[15:22] Sara: agreed. we can top up if outcome promising.
[15:28] Priya: ok i'm going to enumerate the bench scenarios that fit under $2k: keep run time short (4h per variant), use smaller instance families, and prioritize the most promising model variants (7B distilled, 13B int8). we'll exclude 70B for cost reasons.
[15:48] Malik: fine. on telemetry: what observability will we get? token-level cost breakdown? per-route p95?
[15:56] Jordan: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-model latency, per-route breakdown, KV cache hit rates, and token counts per request. We'll share a demo of those dashboards after the bench.
[16:15] Lina: for enterprise signoff who's the approver for security?
[16:20] Malik: that's me and our security lead — we'll review SOC2 and network diagram.
[16:26] Jordan: we'll include those in the docs packet.
[16:30] Priya: quick aside: for batching knobs we'll test max_batch_size [1,4,8], batch_timeout ms [1,8,20], and pre-warm concurrency to minimize cold starts. these three parameters usually explain most of the latency vs cost tradeoffs.
[16:55] Sara: what's the expected amortization percent for batching at your suggested settings?
[17:02] Priya: empirical: with batch 4 and batch_timeout 8ms we often see 25–35% fewer GPU cycles per token vs batch 1 for short sequences. batch 8 gives 40–55% but tail latency increases.
[17:22] Malik: good. can we see p95 latency vs batch size curves in the bench output?
[17:27] Priya: yes, bench collects latency histograms per batch size and per model.
[17:33] Jordan: i'm going to summarize the POC acceptance criteria we agreed: 
- Realtime triage p95 <= 300ms at expected peak (8 rps sustained, burst to 25 rps)
- Per-session cost on expected load <= $0.05 under the "expected" caching scenario
- Quality: F1 >= baseline + 8% or equivalent business KPIs
- Security: SOC2 docs reviewed and VPC peering approved
[18:05] Lina: yes that aligns.
[18:10] Malik: about the async summarization jobs, what's a reasonable throughput target?
[18:16] Priya: for async we'll target throughput of 200 jobs/hour initially, with p99 latency under 5s not required — we just need cost predictability. we'll include a batch processing profile to show per-job cost.
[18:35] Sara: timeline specifics: can you deliver the bench config by Friday? we want to schedule runs early next week.
[18:42] Priya: yes, will share config and replay template by Friday EOD.
[18:46] Jordan: action: Jordan send spreadsheet + SOC2 links; Priya share bench harness link + run schedule; AlphaHealth to provide anonymized replay by Friday.
[19:00] Malik: ok. couple more detail q's — how do you handle model fallback accounting in cost reports?
[19:08] Priya: bench will report per-request routing path, so cost per effective session will be aggregated including fallback hits. we'll provide a model routing simulation sheet with confidence thresholds and cost impact.
[19:30] Lina: can we simulate an extreme-burst scenario (25 rps sustained for 10 minutes) to see SLOs?
[19:38] Priya: yes, we'll include that as a stress test cell; it will show tail latency and whether autoscaling or fallback is required.
[19:48] Jordan: pricing note: if AlphaHealth moves to Dedicated reserved capacity later, per-token can drop materially but requires commit; we'll show a 3-month and 12-month reserved projection.
[20:02] Malik: fine. what about engineering integration effort estimate?
[20:08] Priya: integration for triage is light — a single HTTP route to Redwood API + minimal retry logic + header for tokenization. expect 2–3 engineer days to integrate in staging. fine-tune + benchmarking add another 3–4 days. we'll enumerate tasks in the doc.
[20:30] Sara: ok good.
[20:34] Priya: i want to call out that caching effectiveness hinges on how templated prompts are. please include a sample of most common prompts in the replay so we can estimate cache hit.
[20:50] Malik: we'll do that.
[20:55] Jordan: any outstanding compliance blockers?
[21:00] Malik: only if we need to cache PHI — that'll be a no-go. otherwise peering and SOC2 are standard checks.
[21:08] Jordan: understood. we'll propose cache-only-for-non-phi and show math.
[21:15] Priya: last technical point: sequence length distribution matters a lot for kernel selection. please share token length histograms. if most triage prompts are <128 tokens we can pick very low-latency kernels.
[21:30] Malik: we'll add that to the replay export.
[21:35] Jordan: ok, time to recap next steps and owners.
[21:40] Jordan: 1) Jordan: send per-token cost spreadsheet, SOC2 + arch diagrams (by 5/16). 2) Priya: bench harness + run schedule + model matrix (by 5/16). 3) AlphaHealth: anonymized replay + token histograms + approval for VPC peering (by 5/16). 4) All: sync 30-min on 5/21 to review initial bench results.
[22:10] Lina: confirmed.
[22:15] Malik: quick question, for the POC how will Redwood invoice or track the $2k budget?
[22:22] Jordan: we'll track usage in the console and send a single POC invoice or credit note depending on the account setup; we'll be transparent on spend and warn if we hit 80% of budget.
[22:36] Sara: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[22:40] Priya: one small note — we'll also include a short playbook with recommended batching/caching knobs per scenario so your engineers can quickly copy them into config.
[22:53] Malik: that's helpful.
[22:57] Jordan: OK wrapping up. we'll follow up with attachments. appreciate the time.
[23:05] Lina: thanks, bye.
[23:08] Malik: thanks.

(Transcript ends — remaining time used for off-record technical follow-ups not transcribed)
